newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end tad higher in range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end tad higher in range-bound trade.

text.p: Select gains recorded by a few index heavyweight stocks on Tuesday helped the benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) rebound in late trade to end slighly higher, dealers said.
"Trading was mostly speculator-driven...choppy price movements," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.

Market-major Tata Iron & Steel Company Ltd (TISCO) was in market focus as speculators were aggressive bidders in the stock. Some buying by foreign funds also helped the share to jump 8.25 rupees, or 4.55 percent, to 189.75 rupees.
TISCO topped the list of the most heavily traded shares.
With more than 7.25 million shares changing hands, TISCO displaced SBI as the top traded stock at the BSE. SBI rose 5.75 rupees to 247.50 in volumes of over five million shares.
"TISCO was the major market mover today...there appears to be quite a lot of speculative pressure," said Piyush Vora, a member-broker of the BSE.
"It is quite rare to see the stock topping the list of most actively traded shares at the BSE," Vora said.
At the rival National Stock Exchange (NSE), TISCO surged 7.05 rupees to end at 187.95 in volumes of 12.2 million shares.
Market participants said foreign funds were keeping a low profile and were scattered buyers in pivotal stocks.
The BSE's benchmark 30-share index closed 12.07 points, or 0.37 percent, higher at 3,264.68 off its intra-day high of 3,273.43.
ACC fell 1.75 rupees to 1,288.0, ITC 2.75 to 323.25, TELCO 5.0 to 348.50, MTNL 2.25 to 228.5 and Gujarat Ambuja 1.0 to 259.
Reliance however advanced 3.0 to 219.0, M&M 5.25 to 352.0 and Sterlite 8.50 to 229.25. REUTER
